13.1 Tangent to a Curve at a Point

blocks.prompt: 1 The slope of the secant line through \(P(x, f(x))\) and \(Q(x + \delta x, f(x + \delta x))\) is
blocks.explanation: Slope = rise over run. Rise \(= f(x+\delta x) - f(x)\), run \(= (x + \delta x) - x = \delta x\).

book_ref.quote: Here \(\delta x\) is the increment in the value of \(x\)

blocks.prompt: 2 As \(\delta x \to 0\), the point \(Q\) approaches \(P\) and the secant line \(PQ\) becomes

options.text: a line parallel to the y-axis

blocks.explanation: The revolving secant turns into the tangent \(PT\) at \(P\); its slope is \(m_{\text{tan}} = \lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{f(x+\delta x)-f(x)}{\delta x}\).

book_ref.quote: the secant line becomes the tangent line

blocks.prompt: 3 Why can we not put \(\delta x = 0\) directly in \(\dfrac{f(x+\delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\)?

options.text: It gives \(\frac{0}{0}\), which has no meaning

blocks.explanation: With \(\delta x = 0\), \(Q\) falls on \(P\): the quotient becomes \(\frac{f(x)-f(x)}{0} = \frac{0}{0}\). So we cancel \(\delta x\) first and then take the limit.

book_ref.quote: To find the slope of a line we need two points, but a tangent touches the curve at only one point

blocks.prompt: 4 The slope of the secant to \(f(x) = x^{2} + 1\) through the points where \(x = 1\) and \(x = 3\) is

book_ref.quote: A secant cuts a curve at two points

blocks.prompt: 5 For \(f(x) = x^{2} + 3x\), the slope of the secant through \(x = 2\) and \(x = 2 + \delta x\) is
blocks.explanation: \(f(2+\delta x) - f(2) = (4 + 4\delta x + \delta x^{2} + 6 + 3\delta x) - 10 = 7\delta x + \delta x^{2}\); dividing by \(\delta x\) gives \(7 + \delta x\).

book_ref.quote: Working pattern: substitute, expand, cancel the common factor

blocks.prompt: 6 The slope of the tangent to \(f(x) = x^{2} + 3x\) at \(x = 2\) is
blocks.explanation: \(m_{\text{tan}} = \lim_{\delta x \to 0}(7 + \delta x) = 7\).

book_ref.quote: We see that \(m_{\text{tan}}\) is the limit of \(m_{\text{sec}}\)

blocks.prompt: 7 The line through \((1, -2)\) with slope \(3\) is
blocks.explanation: \(y - (-2) = 3(x - 1) \Rightarrow y + 2 = 3x - 3 \Rightarrow y = 3x - 5\).

book_ref.quote: To find the equation of a tangent you always need two things

blocks.prompt: 8 The tangent to \(y = x^{2} + 1\) at the point \((1, 2)\) is
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{f(1+\delta x) - f(1)}{\delta x} = 2 + \delta x \to 2\). Then \(y - 2 = 2(x - 1)\), i.e. \(y = 2x\). Check: \(x^{2} + 1 = 2x\) gives \((x-1)^{2} = 0\), one repeated root.

book_ref.quote: the line touches the curve at \(P\) and does not cut it again
